summary:
This is printed page 621 (PDF 645), the final page of the index. The rest of the page is blank.

**How to use it:** numbers are *printed* pages; add 24 for the PDF page.

**Entries**

- **W:** *weights* 9, 39, 596 (PDF 33, 63, 620) with pruning 188 and quantization 188 (PDF 212), regularization 165–166 (PDF 189–190), regularizer instances 165 (PDF 189); *weight.value.grad method* 217 (PDF 241); *wget shell utility* 311 (PDF 335); *while statements* 591 (PDF 615); *Wigner, Eugene* 175 (PDF 199); *Word2Vec* 462–464 (PDF 486–488); *word embeddings* 409, 410 (PDF 433, 434), pretraining 414 (PDF 438); *word tokenization* 387–390 (PDF 411–414); *workflow, machine learning*: framing problem 172–174 (PDF 196–198), collecting dataset 174–177 (PDF 198–201), investing in data-annotation infrastructure 175 (PDF 199), non-representative data 176 (PDF 200), task definition 172–178 (PDF 196–202), choosing measure of success 178 (PDF 202), understanding data 178 (PDF 202).
- **X:** *Xception model* 258, 299 (PDF 282, 323).
- **Y:** *YOLO (You Only Look Once) models*: training from scratch 332 (PDF 356), creating 336 (PDF 360), preparing COCO data for object detection 339 (PDF 363), training 342 (PDF 366).
- **Z:** *zero_grad() method* 217 (PDF 241), the PyTorch call for resetting gradients.

concepts.name: Word embeddings
concepts.definition: Index entry: printed 409, 410 → PDF 433, 434; pretraining 414 → PDF 438; Word2Vec 462–464 → PDF 486–488.
concepts.intuition: Dense vectors for words, learned so that related words end up close together.
concepts.technical: Chapter 14 learns and pretrains embeddings; Word2Vec comes up in the discussion of why Transformers work (chapter 15).
concepts.significance: Embeddings are the input layer of every text model in the book.

concepts.significance: Chapter 6's step-by-step recipe for any ML project.
